descriptionChirho: Aramaic noun denoting clay or ceramic material, used exclusively in Daniel's vision of the statue with feet partly of iron and partly of clay (Dan 2). All 9 occurrences refer to the same material substance — the split into two clusters reflects only grammatical variation (absolute vs. construct state, with/without prepositions b- and w-). Multilingual evidence is uniform: eng 'clay', spa 'barro', hin मिट्टी, arb خَزَف, kor 진흙, swa 'udongo' — all denoting the same earthenware/clay material across both clusters.
